stem: The graph of the linear function \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. Which of the following points lies on the graph of \(y = f(x)\)?
solution: From the labeled points \((0, 2)\) and \((2, 4)\), the slope is \(\frac{4 - 2}{2 - 0} = 1\) and the \(y\)-intercept is 2, so \(f(x) = x + 2\).
Test each point: \(5 + 2 = 7\), so \((5, 7)\) is on the graph; the other points do not satisfy \(y = x + 2\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This swaps the coordinates; \(f(7) = 9\), not 5.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This treats the graph as \(y = 2x\); the graph has slope 1 and \(f(3) = 5\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(f(-2) = -2 + 2 = 0\), not 4; this adds 2 to \(2\) instead of to \(-2\).
explanation.D: Correct. The graph has slope 1 and \(y\)-intercept 2, so \(f(x) = x + 2\), and \(f(5) = 7\).

verify:
x = symbols('x')
f = sympify(figure['curves'][0]['expr'])
assert all(f.subs(x, q['x']) == q['y'] for q in figure['points'])
pt = lambda s: value(s)
ok = [k for k in choices if f.subs(x, pt(choices[k])[0]) == pt(choices[k])[1]]
assert ok == [answer]
